roadmaps.title: Top-5% in 26 engineering domains
roadmaps.description:
Top 5% in all of: CS, DSA, OS, data engineering, data analysis, machine learning, maths, statistics, probability, web development, DevOps, DataOps, Linux, C/C++, Java, Rust, Python, software engineering, Bash, network, API design, containerization (Docker, Podman, Kubernetes), cloud (Google, AWS, Azure), cybersecurity, databases, and database administration.

14 phases, about 3,700 hours at 22 hours a week, from 2026-10-05 to 2030-02-24. Each phase has a project that builds on the previous one, and each domain has an external proof. 22–26 hours a week, 200 € a month (books, a cloud sandbox, a certification fund, a reward fund).

Weekly rhythm: Monday maths, Tuesday CS, Wednesday the language track, Thursday whichever is behind, Friday spaced tests and 3 DSA problems, Saturday 4 h project + 2 h DSA + 1 h notes, Sunday 3 h project + 2 h reading + 1 h Zettel + the weekly reflection.

goal.title: Top-5% in 26 engineering domains
goal.outcome:
By 2030-02-24, every domain has its proof (the full matrix is in the roadmap):

- [ ] CS: nand2tetris 1–12 · CS:APP labs · MIT 6.5840 all labs · Crafting
      Interpreters (jlox + clox) · 18.404 problem sets
- [ ] DSA: ≥ 400 LeetCode problems, contest rating top 5%
- [ ] OS: all xv6 (MIT 6.1810) labs
- [ ] Data engineering: streamhouse in production on K8s · ≥ 3 merged PRs in DE
      OSS
- [ ] Data analysis: 3 published analyses (EDA, viz, dashboard, A/B)
- [ ] Machine learning: Kaggle silver in a 1000+ team competition
- [ ] Maths: 6.042J, 18.01, 18.02, 18.06 finals ≥ 80%
- [ ] Stats: 18.650 final ≥ 80% · Bayesian A/B project
- [ ] Probability: Stat 110 final ≥ 80%
- [ ] Web development: Full Stack Open, all parts
- [ ] DevOps: CKA · DORA-elite pipelines
- [ ] DataOps: contracts + data CI/CD + observability · merged PR in GX or
      OpenLineage
- [ ] Linux: LFCS
- [ ] C/C++: CS:APP labs · all BusTub projects · sqlc-cpp clang-tidy clean
- [ ] Java: OCP Java SE 21 (1Z0-830)
- [ ] Rust: rustkv · merged PR in a Rust project
- [ ] Python: pipekit on PyPI · merged PRs in Python OSS
- [ ] Software engineering: public design docs + reviewed OSS PRs
- [ ] Bash: OverTheWire Bandit 0–33 · tested ShellCheck-clean library
- [ ] Network: CCNA
- [ ] API design: lint-clean REST + gRPC APIs with a public design doc
- [ ] Containerization: CKA + CKS · rootless Podman pipeline
- [ ] Cloud: AWS SAA + GCP ACE + AZ-104
- [ ] Cybersecurity: BSCP · all PortSwigger labs · MIT 6.566 labs
- [ ] Databases: all CMU 15-445 projects · advanced SQL portfolio
- [ ] Database administration: PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, Redis, Cassandra
      runbooks with recorded drills

## Why it matters

Moving from "data engineer who uses the tools" to an engineer who masters every
layer, with external proof for each.

phases.title: Phase 1: Python, DSA I, discrete maths, Bash & Linux CLI
phases.tracks: M = MIT 6.042J discrete maths · C = MIT 6.006 algorithms · L = Fluent Python + Cosmic Python · R = TLCL + BashGuide + Missing Semester

project.title: pipekit: mini orchestrator in Python
project.outcome: Pip-installable mini Airflow: DAG model, topo-sort scheduler, retries, CLI, plugins. mypy strict, pytest + hypothesis ≥ 90% coverage, GitHub Actions CI, Cosmic Python architecture.

exit.title: pipekit v0.1 released, CI green, coverage ≥ 90%
6.042J proofs, counting, and graph problem sets done

fortytwo.title: ready_set_boole
fortytwo.note: Boolean algebra and sets, pairs with 6.042J.

fortytwo.title: 42 Python piscine modules, checked with Germinette

phases.title: Phase 2: Computer architecture, C & systems, DSA II, calculus
phases.tracks: M = 18.01SC → 18.02SC calculus (+ Exo7) · C = CS:APP + labs; Nand to Tetris 1–6 · L = Modern C · R = Erickson Algorithms

project.title: colstore-c: columnar storage in C
project.outcome: CSV → columnar binary (mmap, dictionary/RLE), benchmarked against pandas and DuckDB. Built on your own libft + get_next_line.

exit.title: colstore-c handles 1 GB CSV, ASan + valgrind clean, benchmark write-up

fortytwo.title: push_swap
fortytwo.note: Sorting with two stacks, within the 42 move limits.

phases.title: Phase 3: Operating systems, network theory, linear algebra, probability I
phases.tracks: M = 18.06SC linear algebra; Stat 110 first half · C = OSTEP + xv6 labs · L = Kurose & Ross + Beej sockets in C

project.title: tinyhttpd: an HTTP server in C
project.outcome: An epoll + thread-pool HTTP/1.1 server in C that ingests into colstore; load-tested. Follows the 42 webserv spec (config file, multiple ports, CGI).

exit.title: All MIT 6.1810 xv6 labs pass make grade

fortytwo.title: philosophers
fortytwo.note: Threads and mutexes, no data races under -fsanitize=thread.

phases.title: Phase 4: Linux administration, network operations, Bash automation, probability II
phases.tracks: M = Stat 110 second half · C = ULSAH Linux administration + LFCS prep · L = CCNA (Jeremy's IT Lab + Packet Tracer); Bash library

project.title: homelab-infra: a routed, segmented homelab
project.outcome: 3+ Linux VMs on a routed/VLAN-segmented virtual network: DNS, DHCP, firewall, WireGuard VPN, NFS and LVM, monitoring and log shipping, all provisioned by a tested, ShellCheck-clean Bash library (bats tests).

exit.title: homelab rebuilt from scratch by one script

phases.title: Phase 5: Database internals, PostgreSQL DBA, Rust, statistics
phases.tracks: M = MIT 18.650 statistics · C = CMU 15-445 + BusTub; DDIA · L = Rust Book + Rustlings; PostgreSQL 14 Internals

project.title: rustkv: an LSM key-value store in Rust
project.outcome: WAL, SSTables, bloom filters, compaction, crash recovery. Plus a PostgreSQL lab: replication, failover, PITR, tuning.

exit.title: All BusTub projects pass local tests
rustkv crash-recovery test passes; benchmark write-up

phases.title: Phase 6: Advanced SQL, polyglot DBA, distributed systems, Bayesian stats
phases.tracks: M = Think Bayes 2 · C = MIT 6.5840 distributed systems (Go) · L = Use The Index, Luke + MySQL/MongoDB/Redis/Cassandra DBA

project.title: raft-polystore: Raft and a polyglot DBA lab
project.outcome: All 6.5840 labs (sharded fault-tolerant KV). Plus a DBA lab for MySQL (replication, backup), MongoDB (replica set), Redis (sentinel/cluster), and Cassandra (3 nodes, repair), each with a runbook and a recorded failure drill.

exit.title: All 6.5840 labs pass repeated test runs
5 DBA runbooks with recorded failover/restore drills
30 hard SQL problems (windows, recursive CTEs, plan analysis)

phases.title: Phase 7: Advanced data engineering, DataOps, data analysis & experimentation
phases.tracks: M = Think Stats + Kohavi experimentation · C = Fundamentals of DE + Kafka/Spark/Iceberg docs · L = Python for Data Analysis + Wilke dataviz; GX + OpenLineage

project.title: streamhouse: a streaming lakehouse
project.outcome: Kafka → Spark → Iceberg → dbt → DuckDB/Trino, with a DataOps layer (data contracts, GX, OpenLineage, data CI/CD, freshness/volume SLOs), a BI dashboard, and 3 published analyses (EDA, viz, A/B with power analysis).

exit.title: make up runs the full platform
A broken data contract fails CI
First OSS PR opened in a DE/DataOps project

fortytwo.title: Data Science Piscine
fortytwo.note: PostgreSQL in docker compose, ETL, warehouse, analysis: the warm-up before streamhouse.

phases.title: Phase 8: Containers, Kubernetes, DevOps, AWS
phases.tracks: M = SRE books (SLOs, error budgets) · C = Kubernetes docs + Kubernetes The Hard Way · L = Terraform + Docker/Podman; AWS SAA prep

project.title: streamhouse-on-k8s: GitOps on Kubernetes
project.outcome: k3s → EKS via Terraform, GitOps, rootless Podman builds, Prometheus/Grafana, SLOs, DORA metrics.

exit.title: Cluster rebuilt from zero in under 30 min, then destroyed

fortytwo.title: Inception
fortytwo.note: NGINX + TLS, WordPress, MariaDB in hand-written Dockerfiles: the first week of the phase.

phases.title: Phase 9: Google Cloud, Azure, multi-cloud & platform engineering
phases.tracks: M = DevOps Handbook + cloud cost modeling · C = GCP: Google Skills + ACE guide · L = Azure: AZ-104 learning paths; Terraform GCP/Azure

project.title: multicloud-streamhouse: one codebase, three clouds
project.outcome: One Terraform codebase deploying streamhouse to GKE (BigQuery/GCS), AKS (ADLS), and EKS, with a cost and an IAM/networking comparison write-up.

phases.title: Phase 10: Software engineering, API design, web development, Java
phases.tracks: M = SWE at Google + A Philosophy of Software Design · C = Google AIPs + Zalando API guidelines · L = Java: dev.java + Effective Java + OCP prep · R = Full Stack Open

project.title: datacatalog: a data catalog with lineage
project.outcome: Spring Boot REST + gRPC (AIP-style), React/TS front end, auth, OpenLineage ingestion, on the clusters.

exit.title: Full Stack Open certificate, all parts
API spec lint-clean vs Zalando/AIP rules + public design doc
Catalog shows lineage from a real streamhouse run

fortytwo.title: ft_transcendence
fortytwo.note: A real-time multiplayer web app with a team: only if you're ahead.

phases.title: Phase 11: Machine learning & MLOps, maths for ML
phases.tracks: M = MML book + CS229 notes · C = ISLP + Zero to Hero · L = Hands-On ML (PyTorch) + Designing ML Systems; fast.ai

project.title: ml-on-streamhouse: ML in production
project.outcome: Feature pipeline, experiment tracking, serving via datacatalog, drift monitoring, and a Kaggle competition.

exit.title: Model in production with drift dashboard

phases.title: Phase 12: Cybersecurity, network security, container security
phases.tracks: M = threat modeling + crypto (6.566 lectures) · C = MIT 6.566 labs · L = PortSwigger Academy → BSCP; CKS prep; OverTheWire

project.title: secure-streamhouse: threat model and pentest
project.outcome: Threat model, pentest, hardening (SAST/DAST, network policies, secrets, IAM least privilege) on all 3 clouds.

exit.title: Pentest report, all high findings fixed

phases.title: Phase 13: C++, compilers, theory of computation
phases.tracks: M = MIT 18.404J theory of computation · C = Crafting Interpreters; Nand to Tetris 7–12 · L = LearnCpp + A Tour of C++ + C++ Core Guidelines

project.title: sqlc-cpp: a SQL compiler in modern C++
project.outcome: Lexer, parser, planner, and bytecode VM that runs on colstore files, compared with DuckDB.

fortytwo.title: CPP modules 00–09
fortytwo.note: Classes, polymorphism, templates, STL, before sqlc-cpp.

phases.title: Phase 14: Mastery & proof
phases.tracks: M = weakest maths/theory domain from monthly tests · C = LeetCode contests + Kaggle · L = OSS PRs + portfolio write-ups

project.title: oss-and-portfolio: proof of every domain
project.outcome: Weekly LeetCode contests, a Kaggle silver push, at least 3 merged OSS PRs (DE, Rust/Python, DataOps), and a portfolio site with 14 project write-ups. Retake any failed exam.

habits.title: Daily study block
habits.stack: After dinner on weekdays; at 09:00 on weekends
habits.cue: At the desk, the phone in another room.
habits.craving: Small daily compounding beats heroic weekends.
habits.two: Open today's first task and do one 25-minute pomodoro: a day counts after 25 focused minutes.
habits.reward: Tick the day and watch the streak grow; +1 rest token every 6 study days (bank up to 4), and streak rewards from the 20 € fund.
habits.identity: I'm someone who studies every day.

habits.title: Daily review: spaced tests and the board
habits.stack: When I sit down for the study block, before new material
habits.craving: Retrieval and spacing make 2.5 years of material stick; without them, phase 1 is gone by phase 4.
habits.two: Answer the oldest due test, then move today's tasks to Doing (15 minutes at most).
habits.reward: A cleared board; new material only once the old is retrieved.

habits.title: Weekly project deep-work session
habits.cue: No notifications, the current phase project open.
habits.craving: Projects turn reading into skill and build the portfolio that proves the top 5%.
habits.two: Pick one project task and run the tests; aim for a 4-hour block that ends with a commit.
habits.reward: Push to GitHub and enjoy the green CI badge; a finished feature earns the afternoon off from theory.

habits.title: Weekly reflection and roadmap check
habits.stack: Sunday, the last hour of the weekend block
habits.craving: A 2.5-year plan only survives if it's re-planned every week.
habits.two: Hours done against 22, what I learned, what's stuck, the token bank, next week's 5–8 tasks. Last Sunday of the month: the roadmap check.

resources.title: 42 subjects and testers
resources.description:
Never copy solutions; read others' code only after yours passes.

- Subjects: ALL_SCHOOL_42 (last updated 2022: check each subject's version)
- Newer subjects and testers: GitHub topics 42 (https://github.com/topics/42) and 42-cursus (https://github.com/topics/42-cursus)
- Exam practice: 42_examshell, ranks 02–06 (https://github.com/terminal-42s/42_examshell)
- A 42-like environment: 42-Devcontainer (https://github.com/opsec-infosec/42-Devcontainer)
- Python projects checker: Germinette (https://github.com/ExceptedPrism3/germinette)
- To compare after yours passes: mcombeau/42_cursus_projects (https://github.com/mcombeau/42_cursus_projects)
- Not covered by 42: Java, Rust, and database administration, which come from the phase resources.

resources.title: Certification exams
resources.description:
About $3,000 of exams over 3.4 years, paid from the 100 €/month certification fund. Watch for Linux Foundation discounts.

- LFCS $445 (phase 4)
- CCNA $300 (phase 4)
- CKA $445 (phase 8)
- AWS SAA $150 (phase 8)
- GCP ACE $125 (phase 9)
- AZ-104: check the price for your region (phase 9)
- Oracle 1Z0-830 $245 (phase 10)
- BSCP $99, plus a Burp Pro subscription (phase 12)
- CKS $445 (phase 12)

resources.title: Books platform
resources.description: O'Reilly access through the ACM + Skills Bundle ($75 a year), or O'Reilly directly (https://www.oreilly.com/online-learning/pricing): about 10 € a month.
